evals.name: silent-catch-detection
evals.expected_output: Flag CRITICAL — silent error swallowing via .catch(() => {}). Registry reconstitution failures will be invisible. Fix: .catch(e => console.error('[server] reconstitution failed:', e))
evals.root_cause_tested: silent-catch — tests whether skill detects .catch(() => {}) pattern and flags as CRITICAL (real bug from cmuxlayer PR #21)

assertions.name: identifies_silent_catch
assertions.description: Identifies .catch(() => {}) as a security issue (silent error swallowing)

assertions.name: severity_critical
assertions.description: Rates the finding as CRITICAL severity, not just a warning

assertions.name: provides_fix
assertions.description: Recommends logging the error (console.error or similar) instead of swallowing

evals.name: unsanitized-exec-detection
evals.expected_output: Flag CRITICAL — unsanitized shell command execution. Both inputPath and format are interpolated into a shell string via execSync. An attacker could inject shell commands. Fix: use array-based exec or validate/sanitize inputs.
evals.root_cause_tested: unsanitized-exec — tests detection of template literal interpolation in execSync (real pattern from voicelayer SafeSkill scan, 52 critical findings)

assertions.name: identifies_shell_injection
assertions.description: Identifies template literal interpolation in execSync as shell injection risk

assertions.name: severity_critical
assertions.description: Rates as CRITICAL, not medium or low

assertions.name: recommends_array_args
assertions.description: Recommends array-based arguments or input sanitization as the fix

assertions.name: identifies_both_inputs
assertions.description: Identifies both inputPath AND format as injection vectors, not just one

evals.name: path-traversal-detection
evals.expected_output: Flag HIGH — path traversal vulnerability. User-controlled filePath joined with base directory without validation. Input '../../etc/passwd' would escape /data. Fix: path.resolve + startsWith check.
evals.root_cause_tested: path-traversal — tests detection of unvalidated path.join with user input (real pattern from orchestrator PR #41)

assertions.name: identifies_path_traversal
assertions.description: Identifies path.join with user input as path traversal risk

assertions.name: shows_exploit
assertions.description: Demonstrates the exploit (e.g., ../../etc/passwd or similar traversal)

assertions.name: recommends_resolve_check
assertions.description: Recommends path.resolve + startsWith boundary check

evals.name: tool-annotations-audit
evals.expected_output: All 3 tools missing ToolAnnotations. list_files: readOnlyHint=true, destructiveHint=false. delete_file: readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=true, idempotentHint=false. get_status: readOnlyHint=true, destructiveHint=false, idempotentHint=true.
evals.root_cause_tested: tool-annotations — tests whether skill audits ToolAnnotations coverage and recommends correct values per MCP spec

assertions.name: identifies_all_missing
assertions.description: Identifies all 3 tools as missing ToolAnnotations

assertions.name: delete_destructive
assertions.description: Correctly marks delete_file as destructiveHint=true

assertions.name: get_status_readonly
assertions.description: Correctly marks get_status as readOnlyHint=true

assertions.name: uses_mcp_spec_fields
assertions.description: Uses actual MCP spec annotation field names (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint)

evals.name: hardcoded-secrets-detection
evals.expected_output: Flag CRITICAL — hardcoded secrets. api_key contains what appears to be a real Anthropic API key (sk-ant-). admin_password is hardcoded. Flag HIGH — backup_token has a hardcoded fallback that looks like a real token. Fix: use environment variables or 1Password op CLI for all secrets.
evals.root_cause_tested: hardcoded-secrets — tests detection of committed credentials in config objects

assertions.name: identifies_api_key
assertions.description: Flags the hardcoded api_key starting with sk-ant- as a committed secret

assertions.name: identifies_password
assertions.description: Flags admin_password as hardcoded credential

assertions.name: flags_fallback_token
assertions.description: Flags the backup_token fallback value as a potential hardcoded secret

assertions.name: recommends_env_or_vault
assertions.description: Recommends environment variables or secret manager (1Password/vault)

evals.name: json-parse-crash
evals.expected_output: Flag HIGH — unguarded JSON.parse on user input. Malformed JSON will throw and crash the tool handler (potentially the MCP server). Also: config.settings access without null check. Fix: wrap in try/catch, validate parsed structure.
evals.root_cause_tested: json-parse — tests detection of unguarded JSON.parse on tool input in MCP handlers

assertions.name: identifies_unguarded_parse
assertions.description: Identifies JSON.parse without try/catch as a crash risk

assertions.name: mentions_malformed_input
assertions.description: Notes that malformed JSON from tool input will crash the handler

assertions.name: recommends_try_catch
assertions.description: Recommends try/catch wrapper with structured error response

evals.name: ssml-injection-detection
evals.expected_output: Flag MEDIUM — SSML injection. User-controlled text is interpolated directly into SSML template without escaping. Malicious input like '</prosody></speak><audio src="evil.mp3"/>' could inject arbitrary SSML. Fix: escape <>&"' chars before interpolation.
evals.root_cause_tested: ssml-injection — tests detection of user input in SSML templates (voicelayer-specific pattern)

assertions.name: identifies_ssml_injection
assertions.description: Identifies user text interpolated into SSML as an injection risk

assertions.name: shows_exploit_example
assertions.description: Demonstrates or describes how SSML tags in user input could be exploited

assertions.name: recommends_escaping
assertions.description: Recommends HTML/XML entity escaping for special characters

evals.name: structured-output-format
evals.expected_output: Structured audit table with: (1) CRITICAL: run_cmd executes arbitrary commands from tool input, (2) HIGH: read has unvalidated path access, (3) CRITICAL: silent catch on registry.init(), (4) MEDIUM: both tools missing ToolAnnotations. Summary with counts. Verdict: FAIL.
evals.root_cause_tested: structured-output — tests whether skill produces the correct audit output format with severity table, counts, and verdict

assertions.name: uses_table_format
assertions.description: Uses a structured table format with columns for severity, file, pattern, finding

assertions.name: finds_all_four_issues
assertions.description: Identifies all 4 distinct issues: arbitrary exec, unvalidated path, silent catch, missing annotations

assertions.name: correct_severity_ranking
assertions.description: Ranks arbitrary exec and silent catch as CRITICAL, path as HIGH, annotations as MEDIUM

assertions.name: includes_verdict
assertions.description: Includes a clear FAIL verdict given the CRITICAL findings

assertions.name: includes_summary_counts
assertions.description: Includes summary with severity counts (e.g., Critical: 2, High: 1, Medium: 1)
